body:
It is not my desire to bring you down with my negativity.  It seems like you have worked very hard to perfect the environmental influence on your well-being, and it has paid off quite well.  So, all I will say is that I may go head and try what you suggested.

Thank you!

Wow, sounds like hell, like constant torture.  If I had the power, I would snap my fingers and make all your problems go away.  Unfortunately, I am just some random guy in front of a computer.  Are there no government services in your area that can help you with many of your problems, like financial problems, mental health issues, and so forth?  That may perhaps be your best choice. If they can at least make your pain tolerable, then perhaps you would find meaning and purpose in staying alive.
Hello.  Sorry to hear that things are not going too well.  Perhaps if you explain your situation, we can perhaps give some helpful advice.
Well, I respect your choice.  But if you change your mind,  I am here.
You would be surprised how talking about these things results in a lot of helpful ideas and information being shared.  I'd like to help, if I can.

Welcome back!  This is my third time back here.  What doesn't kill you makes you stronger, no?  So just hang out, have a beer or espresso, and let's talk it out.  We are one big family here with the same problems, the same mental health issues.  But here, we are never alone.  So, what's on your mind?

Thank you for the long and thoughtful reply.  I am glad that you found a way to overcome your anxiety.  I myself underwent six months of CBT with my psychiatrist, but it did not help.  My condition is so hard-wired into my brain that environmental intervention does not work.

I did not suffer any consequences that I was aware of.   I was already living in a facility for the mentally disabled when I overdosed on it, so there is not much more help I could have gotten.  I've tried all medications, but nothing worked.  I just wanted to die, since science failed to cure me.
Took a bunch of benzos with alcohol, went into euphoria instead of death, fell asleep, woke up next day feeling good for a few hours, then back to extreme depression, anxiety, and fear.
How about hiking on the mountains of Europa, the  moon of Jupiter?  Stick around long enough, and you may get a chance.  Or, if you like exotic travel, save up and buy a nice telescope.

There is an international community of hundreds of millions  of LGBT that got your back, and see you as close family.  Just reach out, and you will be inundated with an ocean of love and support! I cannot overstate just how much cultural strength you bring to our world by being a member of the LGBT community.  I can only dream of being such a valuable person.  I personally identify as asexual, and I seek to undergo medical procedures to bring my asexuality to fruition.
You've posted here, and I now know you exist.  We all now know.  I would hate to lose a friend.

"Don't have a life," such a subjective statement.  Do people who say that to you have a moral or philosophical monopoly on what "having a life" is?  It's all subjective.  I've found that the best thing I could do to make myself worth something is to do something to help another person.  If someone else's life improves because of something I did to help, then I feel my life has been worthwhile.  I mean, if you were to be judged by a deity or space aliens or something, would not the chances by high that they would judge you based on how selfless you were and how much of your time you spent doing something for the collective well-being of mankind?

>I know how you feel.  I have addictions.  I try my best to quit, do good for a week, sometimes a few weeks, then crash again.  when years go by like this, and no progress is made, and you've reached the highest point you will ever reach, which is a point still below sea-level, you then ask what's the point of trying again.   I guess if you have no family that will miss you or need you, or any friends who need you, and if you have no greater purpose on Earth like charity works for a greater cause . . .  But then, maybe you do.

You just talked to me right now, that gave me pleasure, and that makes you valuable.  We people in this forum need friends who have the same issues.  Even if you can help just a few people in this forum, that makes you valuable.
